topics.title: Page 1
topics.context:
The NASA STI Program...in Profile

Since its founding, NASA has been dedicated to the advancement of aeronautics and space science. The NASA Scientific and Technical Information (STI) Program Office plays a key part in helping NASA maintain this important role.

The NASA STI Program Office is operated by Langley Research Center, the lead center for NASA's scientific and technical information. The NASA STI Program Office provides access to the NASA STI Database, the largest collection of aeronautical and space science STI in the world. The Program Office is also NASA's institutional mechanism for disseminating the results of its research and development activities. These results are published by NASA in the NASA STI Report Series, which includes the following report types:

  • TECHNICAL PUBLICATION. Reports of completed research or a major significant phase of research that present the results of NASA programs and include extensive data or theoretical analysis. Includes compilations of significant scientific and technical data and information deemed to be of continuing reference value. NASA's counterpart of peer-reviewed formal professional papers but has less stringent limitations on manuscript length and extent of graphic presentations.
  • TECHNICAL MEMORANDUM. Scientific and technical findings that are preliminary or of specialized interest, e.g., quick release reports, working papers, and bibliographies that contain minimal annotation. Does not contain extensive analysis.
  • CONTRACTOR REPORT. Scientific and technical findings by NASA-sponsored contractors and grantees.
  • CONFERENCE PUBLICATION. Collected papers from scientific and technical conferences, symposia, seminars, or other meetings sponsored or cosponsored by NASA.
  • SPECIAL PUBLICATION. Scientific, technical, or historical information from NASA programs, projects, and mission, often concerned with subjects having substantial public interest.
  • TECHNICAL TRANSLATION. English-language translations of foreign scientific and technical material pertinent to NASA's mission.

Specialized services that complement the STI Program Office's diverse offerings include creating custom thesauri, building customized databases, organizing and publishing research results...even providing videos.

For more information about the NASA STI Program Office, see the following:

  • Access the NASA STI program home page at <http://www.sti.nasa.gov>
  • E-mail your question via the Internet to <help@sti.nasa.gov>
  • Phone the NASA STI Help Desk at 757-864-9658
  • Write to:
    NASA STI Information Desk
    Mail Stop 148
    NASA Langley Research Center
    Hampton, VA 23681-2199, USA

faqs.question: What is the primary role of the NASA Scientific and Technical Information (STI) Program Office?
faqs.answer: The NASA STI Program Office helps NASA maintain its role in advancing aeronautics and space science by providing access to the NASA STI Database and disseminating the results of NASA's research and development activities.

faqs.question: Which NASA center operates the STI Program Office?
faqs.answer: The Langley Research Center operates the NASA STI Program Office.

faqs.question: What is the NASA STI Database?
faqs.answer: It is the largest collection of aeronautical and space science scientific and technical information in the world.

faqs.question: What types of reports are included in the NASA STI Report Series?
faqs.answer: The series includes Technical Publication, Technical Memorandum, Contractor Report, Conference Publication, Special Publication, and Technical Translation.

faqs.question: What distinguishes a Technical Publication from other report types?
faqs.answer: A Technical Publication reports completed research or a major phase of research, includes extensive data or theoretical analysis, and is similar to peer‑reviewed professional papers but with less stringent limits on length and graphics.

faqs.question: When would a Technical Memorandum be used?
faqs.answer: A Technical Memorandum is used for preliminary or specialized findings, such as quick release reports, working papers, or bibliographies with minimal annotation, and does not contain extensive analysis.

faqs.question: What services does the STI Program Office offer beyond report publication?
faqs.answer: They provide specialized services such as creating custom thesauri, building customized databases, organizing and publishing research results, and even providing videos.

faqs.question: How can I contact the NASA STI Help Desk?
faqs.answer: You can email help@sti.nasa.gov, call 757‑864‑9658, or write to NASA STI Information Desk, Mail Stop 148, NASA Langley Research Center, Hampton, VA 23681‑2199, USA.

faqs.question: Where can I find more information about the NASA STI Program Office online?
faqs.answer: Visit the NASA STI program home page at http://www.sti.nasa.gov.

faqs.question: What is a Technical Translation in the context of NASA STI reports?
faqs.answer: A Technical Translation is an English‑language translation of foreign scientific and technical material that is relevant to NASA's mission.

summary.title: NASA STI Program Office Overview
summary.long_summary: The NASA Scientific and Technical Information (STI) Program Office, operated by Langley Research Center, is central to NASA’s mission of advancing aeronautics and space science. It manages the world’s largest collection of aeronautical and space science STI through the NASA STI Database, ensuring researchers and the public can access comprehensive data and analyses. The Office also serves as NASA’s institutional mechanism for disseminating research results, publishing them in the NASA STI Report Series. This series includes several report types: Technical Publication (detailed research reports with extensive data), Technical Memorandum (preliminary or specialized findings), Contractor Report (results from NASA-sponsored contractors), Conference Publication (collected papers from NASA-sponsored events), Special Publication (public-interest scientific or historical information), and Technical Translation (English translations of foreign material). Beyond publishing, the STI Office offers specialized services such as custom thesauri creation, tailored database construction, research result organization, and even video production. For further information, users can visit the NASA STI website, email help@sti.nasa.gov, call the help desk at 757‑864‑9658, or write to the NASA STI Information Desk at NASA Langley Research Center, Hampton, VA. This comprehensive suite of resources and services underscores NASA’s commitment to sharing scientific knowledge worldwide.
summary.short_summary: NASA's STI Office provides global aeronautics data and reports
